key_insight: DT-DRO adapts the geometry of a DRO ambiguity set using held-out diagnostic transport, reducing over-conservatism caused by misspecified uncertainty models.
engineering_relevance: This gives engineers a more reliable way to make robust decisions when predictive errors are structured or heavy-tailed, such as in energy and risk-sensitive systems.
method: Use held-out calibration data to diagnose probability misallocation via the conditional probability integral transform CDF.
Translate the diagnostic signal into an outcome-level transport that adjusts both the ambiguity-set center and the ground cost.
Solve the resulting DRO problem through a computationally tractable dual reformulation with valid ambiguity radii and risk guarantees.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports synthetic experiments and a power-outage application showing improved decision quality, especially under structural and tail misspecification.
watch_item: Performance depends on calibration data quality and the accuracy of the diagnostic transport approximation, so noisy or limited hold-out data may weaken the benefit.
paper_title: Calibrating Ambiguity Set via Diagnostic Transport for Distributionally Robust Optimization
